executiveSummary: Posture rises to provisional High 61.4/100 because EIA’s Midwest diesel benchmark increased 6.9% for a second consecutive weekly rise above 5%, crossing the prior public-data trigger. This changes guidance to immediate contract and invoice verification, not a claim of realized Watershed cost or disruption. New EIA electricity and General Mills results restore energy and customer-demand coverage with explicit national/archetype limits. Facility / weather and Cyber / OT remain unassessed; no urgent safety/continuity override is active.
baselineNote: Recorded 17–26 September snapshots provide only ten calendar points, insufficient for 30/90/365-day trend inference. Several intervening components expired before replacement; null is unassessed, not zero. Company exposure remains provisional and Cyber / OT remains unassessed.

observations.title: Midwest diesel crosses the prior escalation trigger
observations.status: Reviewed; S01 severity and persistence increased; guidance changed
observations.finding: EIA reports Midwest on-highway diesel at $6.680/gal for 21 September, up $0.430 or 6.9% from 14 September. This follows the prior week’s 5.1% rise and crosses S01’s public-data trigger.
observations.causalPath: Regional retail diesel benchmark ↑ → applicable carrier fuel surcharge or freight quote ↑ → delivered input/outbound cost and conditional margin or service pressure.
observations.sourceScope: Regional retail benchmark only. No Watershed carrier, contract, surcharge, lane, invoice, customer pass-through or service impact is public.
observations.decision: Increase S01 severity 70→80 and persistence 70→80; retain exposure 75, confidence 70, velocity 80, dependency 80 and substitutability 35. Change guidance to immediate contract/invoice verification; do not activate the urgent safety/continuity override.

observations.title: New EIA release restores energy benchmark coverage on a national basis
observations.status: Reviewed; S10 refreshed with non-comparable national benchmark
observations.finding: EIA reports July 2026 U.S. industrial average revenue of 9.77 cents/kWh, up 4.7% from July 2025. The prior June Illinois/Wisconsin snapshot expired.
observations.causalPath: National industrial electricity benchmark ↑ → possible applicable tariff or supply-contract reset → conditional processing and handling cost for freeze-dried, baked, roasted and popped platforms.
observations.sourceScope: National price proxy, not a state or facility tariff. The revised score must not be interpreted as improvement from the prior state-level series.
observations.decision: Refresh S10 at 13.2/100 with factors 80/50/60/70/35/90/40 and a 25 October expiry; require actual bill and tariff validation.

observations.title: Global CPG archetype reports mixed pet and snack demand
observations.status: Reviewed; S12 refreshed; H2 evidence for and against expanded without confidence change
observations.finding: General Mills reported flat North America Pet sales, low-single-digit pet-treat growth, double-digit cat-food growth, high-single-digit dog-food decline, and a modest retailer-inventory headwind. North America Retail organic sales declined 3%, U.S. Snacks declined mid-single digits, and the annual outlook remains cautious while protein, fiber and pet humanization remain innovation priorities.
observations.causalPath: Archetype brand volumes, retailer inventories and innovation priorities → possible launch briefs, outsourcing appetite and order cadence → conditional Watershed sales pipeline.
observations.sourceScope: Single public-company archetype. No Watershed customer, order, mix, capacity allocation or production relationship is established.
observations.decision: Refresh S12 at 2.8/100; change sales guidance to category-specific pipeline verification. Add balanced H2 evidence and retain H2 confidence at 45, fail count 0 and OPEN outcome.

observations.title: FDA adds food recall notices without a Watershed match
observations.status: Unscored lead; no applicable exposure found
observations.finding: The FDA index lists apple sauce for patulin, alfalfa sprouting seeds for STEC/Salmonella, ground cinnamon for lead, pasta for undeclared shellfish and Greek peppers for possible pest contamination.
observations.causalPath: Only a verified ingredient, supplier, customer, SKU or lot match could create a Watershed quality or continuity pathway.
observations.sourceScope: Rolling, incomplete index. Listed products and firms are not attributed to Watershed, and row dates are not treated as event-onset dates.
observations.decision: Keep unscored. Quality should use normal match procedures only if a specific ingredient, supplier, customer, SKU or lot link emerges.

reviewNotes.challenge: Do the diesel, electricity and CPG releases establish Watershed outcomes?
reviewNotes.revision: No. Each primary observation is separated from inferred company exposure; no supplier, customer, contract, tariff, order, invoice or realized loss is claimed.

reviewNotes.challenge: Were factor changes selected to force a High posture?
reviewNotes.revision: No. S01 severity and persistence rise because the prior >5% weekly trigger was crossed twice consecutively; all other S01 factors stay fixed. S10 changes measurement basis and is explicitly non-comparable. S12 remains low-impact despite higher source confidence.

reviewNotes.challenge: Does nominal road-freight reliance prove surcharge pass-through or service risk?
reviewNotes.revision: No. The stronger action is to reconcile actual surcharge tables, lane mix, invoices and pass-through before operational commitments; the public benchmark alone does not prove cost or service impact.

reviewNotes.challenge: Does national electricity inflation quantify process or line cost?
reviewNotes.revision: No. S10 requires tariffs, demand charges, interval use and kWh per product; no production line, equipment load or state utility is inferred.

reviewNotes.challenge: Do the new FDA entries create a recall or contaminant event for Watershed?
reviewNotes.revision: No. The entries stay unscored until a verified ingredient, supplier, customer, SKU or lot match exists. Normal food-safety escalation remains separate from the executive score.

reviewNotes.challenge: Did new CISA candidates establish installed OT exposure?
reviewNotes.revision: No public asset inventory or product match exists. Cyber / OT remains null rather than zero, and no executive cyber persona is selected.

reviewNotes.challenge: Does the High posture require an urgent override or plant action?
reviewNotes.revision: No. The posture is a cost-risk priority driven by an external benchmark. The urgent override remains null because no safety event, outage, closure, route failure or facility disruption is established.

factorReview.disposition: Changed; prior trigger crossed and two factor increases
factorReview.rationale: Exposure 75: public facility geography makes truck freight plausible, but mode and miles are unmeasured. Severity 80: the benchmark reached $6.680/gal and rose 6.9% in one week. Confidence 70: primary EIA measurement, with no company contract or invoice. Persistence 80: two consecutive weekly increases above 5%, supported by the separate EIA distillate-constraint scenario. Velocity 80: weekly repricing can reach surcharges quickly. Dependency 80 and substitutability 35: road freight is operationally important and near-term fuel substitution is limited, but actual carrier terms are unknown.
factorReview.scopeLimitation: Regional retail benchmark; company surcharge, lane, contract, pass-through and service effects unverified.
factorReview.prudentAction: CFO and Supply Chain should reconcile current carrier surcharge tables and invoices, estimate next-cycle margin and OTIF exposure, and confirm customer pass-through before new commitments.
factorReview.strongerResponseTrigger: A third consecutive >5% weekly rise, actual contracted transport cost >5% above plan, a tender/service refusal, or a verified customer-service impact.

factorReview.rationale: Broad grain balance → potential feed/grain pricing → formula costs. All seven factors are uncalibrated proxies (45/55/45/80/45/55/60); popping-grade corn and food-grade contracts can diverge materially.
factorReview.scopeLimitation: No new primary evidence changed company exposure, severity, persistence, velocity, dependency or substitutability. Existing direction, confidence, owners, actions and triggers remain.
factorReview.prudentAction: Track supplier quotations before changing coverage or formulations.
factorReview.strongerResponseTrigger: Two relevant supplier quotes worsen >10%, or verified cover falls below the approved operating threshold.

factorReview.scopeLimitation: No new primary evidence changed company exposure, severity, persistence, velocity, dependency or substitutability. Existing direction, confidence, owners, actions and triggers remain.
factorReview.prudentAction: Quality and IT should map covered inputs and data exchanges, retaining product-specific legal review.
factorReview.strongerResponseTrigger: Final regulatory change, customer deadline, or a confirmed gap in an applicable traceability process.

factorReview.scopeLimitation: No new primary evidence changed company exposure, severity, persistence, velocity, dependency or substitutability. Existing direction, confidence, owners, actions and triggers remain.

factorReview.prudentAction: Confirm the production milestone before offering new formats or delivery commitments.
factorReview.strongerResponseTrigger: Verified commissioned capacity plus a qualified customer opportunity.

factorReview.rationale: SKU classification → applicable contaminant requirements/customer specifications → testing and release criteria. Low velocity 20 reflects an existing rule, not new contamination. Other factors are analytical prioritization.
factorReview.scopeLimitation: No new primary evidence changed company exposure, severity, persistence, velocity, dependency or substitutability. Existing direction, confidence, owners, actions and triggers remain.
factorReview.prudentAction: Keep contaminant controls; have Quality document the correct guidance scope by SKU.
factorReview.strongerResponseTrigger: Changed FDA/state requirements or an actual out-of-spec result; then use the approved food-safety response process.

factorReview.rationale: Exposure falls from 85 to 60 because the county-zone outlook includes the three public municipalities while activity is concentrated especially near and south of I-72, south of the confirmed municipalities; severity falls from 55 to 35 because NWS says severe storms are not expected but lightning remains possible; confidence remains 80 because the primary outlook and SAME-code check are current while site impact is unknown; persistence falls from 40 to 25 because storms are expected to taper by early afternoon and no hazards are expected Tuesday through Sunday; velocity remains 80 because any effect is same-day; dependency and substitutability remain 70/70 pending actual shift, route and scheduling information. These are provisional judgments, not measured disruption.
factorReview.scopeLimitation: Current alert candidates were outside known Illinois facility counties; Wisconsin remains region-only. No site, route, utility or shift impact is established.
factorReview.prudentAction: No additional response is supported beyond normal weather procedures and checking current site and route conditions before affected dispatch or outdoor work.
factorReview.strongerResponseTrigger: A warning matching an operating location, verified route closure, utility interruption or reported site impact warrants immediate reassessment and the approved continuity response.

factorReview.rationale: Exposure 60: advertised platforms imply plausible input channels, not measured spend. Severity 50: material benchmark moves with offsets. Confidence 60: primary data but unknown purchase basis. Persistence 65: possible contract lag; velocity 50: one monthly observation. Dependency 65: ingredient relevance; substitutability 65: broad alternatives subject to quality/customer approval. All factors are provisional judgments.
factorReview.scopeLimitation: No new primary evidence changed company exposure, severity, persistence, velocity, dependency or substitutability. Existing direction, confidence, owners, actions and triggers remain.
factorReview.prudentAction: Compare the next quotes for grain, seed and dairy categories separately; quantify net effect only after purchasing weights are supplied.
factorReview.strongerResponseTrigger: A relevant delivered quote rises >5% against plan or confirmed pass-through fails to offset a sustained input increase.

factorReview.rationale: Exposure 65: relevant regional operating presence. Severity 45: labor-market context without company vacancies. Confidence 45 in the conditional channel, reduced by metro aggregation and seasonality. Persistence 65 and velocity 30: lagged monthly data. Dependency 65: manufacturing staffing. Substitutability 65: unmeasured local alternatives. These are judgments, not a shortage estimate.
factorReview.scopeLimitation: No new primary evidence changed company exposure, severity, persistence, velocity, dependency or substitutability. Existing direction, confidence, owners, actions and triggers remain.
factorReview.prudentAction: Use metro data to frame a hiring review; compare it with actual recruiting results before changing staffing or pay assumptions.
factorReview.strongerResponseTrigger: Critical maintenance/production roles remain unfilled >45 days or persistent overtime exceeds the approved site plan.

factorReview.disposition: Changed; new national benchmark and revised measurement basis
factorReview.rationale: Exposure 80: Watershed advertises energy-dependent processing platforms, but kWh and tariffs are unknown. Severity 50: the national industrial benchmark is 4.7% higher year over year. Confidence 60: primary EIA data, discounted because a national average does not establish Illinois, Wisconsin or facility billing. Persistence 70: monthly cost-planning relevance without proof of contract reset. Velocity 35: lagged July data. Dependency 90: process energy is necessary. Substitutability 40: near-term process-energy alternatives may be limited, while tariff and efficiency options are unverified.
factorReview.scopeLimitation: National price proxy; not comparable to the prior state benchmark and not a Watershed bill.
factorReview.prudentAction: Finance and operations should compare actual effective cents/kWh and process energy use with plan; use the national series only as a screening benchmark.
factorReview.strongerResponseTrigger: Actual effective energy cost exceeds plan by >10% for two billing periods or an applicable utility/grid notice creates a verified continuity concern.

factorReview.rationale: Exposure 65: plausible film/carton dependence with specifications unknown. Severity 55: paperboard increase amid plastic monthly relief. Confidence 60: public indices but uncertain conversion into quotes. Persistence 65 and velocity 45: monthly changes and potential contract lag. Dependency 65: packaging requirement; substitutability 60: specification and customer approvals. Provisional analyst judgments.
factorReview.scopeLimitation: No new primary evidence changed company exposure, severity, persistence, velocity, dependency or substitutability. Existing direction, confidence, owners, actions and triggers remain.
factorReview.prudentAction: Separate carton and film quote reviews; request evidence for index-linked adjustments rather than applying a blended packaging inflation rate.
factorReview.strongerResponseTrigger: Delivered packaging quotes exceed plan by >5% or a qualified vendor reports a material lead-time increase.

factorReview.rationale: Exposure 50: a relevant global CPG/pet archetype with no established Watershed account relationship. Severity 45: mixed category results and inventory pressure, not a confirmed order change. Confidence 70: primary quarterly disclosure, discounted for single-company and portfolio mismatch. Persistence 70: full-year outlook and inventory commentary. Velocity 35: quarterly evidence. Dependency 50: actual customer mix is unknown. Substitutability 70: multiple customer segments and platforms may diversify demand. Factors remain intentionally low for company impact.
factorReview.scopeLimitation: One archetype; no current customer, order or category-wide result inferred.
factorReview.prudentAction: Sales and R&D should compare current qualified briefs with the mixed archetype signals, emphasizing validated pet-treat and protein/fiber problems while testing for snack or dog-food inventory drag before allocating capacity.
factorReview.strongerResponseTrigger: A verified customer changes orders, two additional primary archetypes corroborate the same volume/inventory move, or a qualified launch brief matches available capacity and validated controls.

factorReview.rationale: Exposure 65: global petroleum can affect domestic trucking without direct imports. Severity 70: distillate constraint scenario. Confidence 60: agency forecast, uncertain evolution. Persistence 80: year-end scenario; velocity 65: recent fuel moves. Dependency 75: conditional freight channel; substitutability 50: route/carrier choices do not fully replace diesel. Same fuel-cost issue group as S01; never added to it.
factorReview.scopeLimitation: No new primary evidence changed company exposure, severity, persistence, velocity, dependency or substitutability. Existing direction, confidence, owners, actions and triggers remain.
factorReview.prudentAction: Use the same logistics/finance review as S01; run a conditional fuel-surcharge sensitivity instead of issuing a separate geopolitical alarm.
factorReview.strongerResponseTrigger: The observed relevant diesel benchmark or a contracted surcharge breaches the S01 trigger, or verified lane exposure changes.

rechecks.note: Raised S01 severity and persistence after a second consecutive >5% Midwest diesel increase; refreshed national electricity and global CPG archetype components; kept facility/weather and Cyber/OT null and urgent override inactive.
